attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his newsletter, stated in his own voice.

semantics.note: Keeps the 90% revenue share, the roughly 8% S&P 500 weight, and buyers who 'immediately' lose money. A present-tense observation.

contract.note: Using the latest quarter or the fiscal year for the revenue share, and the index weight at publication, are ordinary readings. 'Immediately lose money' is undefined, so its loss measure is the evaluator's choice.

evidence.note: NVIDIA's release gives Data Center at about 89.7% of FY26 revenue, and the quarter's figures in the release give about 91.5%. This supports only the 90% part, not the index weight or buyer losses.
AWS segment operating income was positive. That is a different company and metric, and it does not isolate returns on installed NVIDIA hardware, so it neither proves nor refutes buyer losses.

reviews.rationale: The 90% revenue share is supported by NVIDIA's disclosure. The packet has no index-weight record from around April 8, 2026, and no buyer-level evidence of immediate losses from installation. AWS profit is only context. Two of the three parts are unestablished, so the claim is unresolved.

attribution.note: The antecedent repeats Davidov's report, which Zitron flags as unverified. The conditional inference is Zitron's own.

semantics.note: An observation conditional on an unverified antecedent, and the antecedent itself includes 'might'. The condition is preserved.

contract.note: The contract rightly requires the antecedent to be confirmed and says failing to verify it is not contradiction. 'Load-bearing', 'hinges' and 'heavily-inflated' have no thresholds.

evidence.note: Anthropic's S-1, available before the cutoff, says cloud-marketplace revenue is recognised gross. That bears on the gross-booking point but gives nothing on Meta's share, Google's fee rate, or the antecedent.
Contemporaneous news report, citing Forbes, that Anthropic reports revenue gross. It does not verify Meta's usage, Google's specific share, or realized revenue.

reviews.rationale: The consequent depends on Davidov's report, which Zitron calls unverified and which itself says 'might'. Nothing in the packet establishes Meta's token share or that it flows through Google. Under policy, a conditional whose antecedent is unknown is not scored. Gross recognition is confirmed, but the 20%+ fee and the size of any inflation are not.

attribution.note: Zitron's own assertion in his newsletter.

semantics.note: Leaving out the media clause is acceptable. The claim is a conjunction about both companies: billions burned, margins worsening over time, and no path to profit.

contract.note: Reading 'margins that get worse over time' as margins declining is the ordinary reading. The contract rightly separates this from missing a forecast. No margin basis is named, but every basis in the packet points the same way.

evidence.note: The filing's risk factor shows net losses and uncertainty about profitability. The loss figures it gives imply Anthropic's net margin improved from 2024 to 2025. It does not prove there is no path to profitability.

Analysis based on the filing, published before the cutoff: Anthropic's gross margin rose from about −95% in 2024 to 40% in 2025, and rose further in H1 2026. This contradicts worsening margins for Anthropic.

reviews.rationale: The claim says both companies have margins that get worse over time. Anthropic's records show margins improving from 2024 to 2025, on a gross basis and on a net basis from the filing's figures. That falsifies the conjunctive claim. Cash burn and the no-path assertion stay unestablished, and there is no OpenAI data.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his newsletter.

semantics.note: Keeps 'seemingly' on the delay assertion and keeps the construction assertion separate. The warning-sign framing is rhetorical.

contract.note: The contract leaves the company population unresolved and admits that 'vast majority' and the project universe are undefined. Which projects and companies count decides the result.

evidence.note: Pre-post tracker: about 11GW of the 16GW slated for 2026 shows no construction, and 26% of expected capacity slipped in 2025. It measures capacity, not project count, and does not show that nearly all projects are late.

reviews.rationale: No evidence settles 'every company loses money' for any defined population. The tracker reports capacity, not counts. It shows most 2026-slated capacity not under construction, but only about a quarter slipping in 2025, which is not clearly 'seemingly every'. Different metric, so it is unresolved.
